INTRODUCTION



 !                THE YEAR THAT LATVIA’S ENERGY
STATEMENT BY      SYSTEM BECAME INDEPENDENT

THE MANAGEMENT    TECHNOLOGICALLY
BOARD
                  It is now over a year since the Baltic
                  States secured their energy independence.
                  In February 2025, the Baltic energy systems
                  severed their historical energy ties with
                  Russia irreversibly and joined the world's
                  biggest energy system - continental Europe.

                  We synchronised our energy systems with those
                  of Europe almost a year earlier than planned.

SUSTAINABILITY REPORT



THE PARENT COMPANY’S
STRATEGY

The central element of the Parent Company’s strategy
remains the Digital and Green Transformation,
aimed at improving operational efficiency, supporting
development, and reducing environmental impact. These
principles are integrated into all company processes,
with particular attention paid to the assessment of
environmental impacts and sustainable development.

A key priority for AST is the implementation of the
largest energy development project in the Baltics —
synchronisation with continental Europe. As a result,
the energy independence of the Baltic States has been
strengthened, and a competitive ancillary services
market is emerging.

=== pdf p.29 ===
Newly elected members of the Supervisory Board
and the Management Board participate in the
"Board Member Education Programme" organised
by the Baltic Institute of Corporate Governance (BICG).
The programme is based on the corporate governance
principles and recommendations of the International
Finance Corporation (IFC) of the World Bank and
the OECD.

In accordance with the requirements of the Financial
Instruments Market Law, the Parent Company has
prepared a Corporate Governance Report for 2025
(this report has not been verified or audited).
The report is available in AS Augstsprieguma tīkls
on the AST and Nasdaq Baltic websites.

In the Group’s companies, information on gender
representation at the highest management level
is disclosed in accordance with the numerical and
percentage distribution of genders represented in
the respective company’s Supervisory Board, Audit
Committee and Management Board.

Each risk and opportunity was assessed on a five‑point
scale based on its likelihood and potential financial
impact on the company. The likelihood and financial
impact scores were multiplied, and a threshold score of
10 was established for determining the materiality of a
given risk or opportunity (i.e., all risks or opportunities
with a combined score of 10 or above are deemed
material).

In this process, consideration was given to the
company’s dependence on critical resources and
suppliers, as well as the potential impact of negative
consequences on financial indicators. Particular
attention was paid to the value chain, including risks
related to supply chain disruptions or the actions of
business partners, as well as potential changes in the
regulatory framework and their impact on the company’s
financial performance.

The Parent Company and the Subsidiary identified
risks and opportunities separately and later assessed
the potential scale of financial impact, likelihood and
time horizon (short, medium or long term) according
to a unified approach. In this process, the Group’s
companies largely relied on the existing approach to
risk management, which is organised based on the
principles set out in ISO 31000. In 2024, financial

in accordance with legal requirements and internal
procedures that ensure that the rights and interests of
affected communities are taken into account.

Qualitative targets for affected communities are included
in the Group’s sustainability initiatives and internal
procedures. These include:

• Mitigating adverse impacts: The Group strives to
  minimise its impact on the environment and society by
  adhering to the highest standards and using the best
  available technologies;

• Promoting positive impacts: The Group promotes
  knowledge and understanding of local communities
  about energy supply and energy security by engaging
  in public education activities;

• Risk and opportunity management: The Group
  identifies and manages risks and opportunities
  related to affected communities to ensure sustainable
  development.

The Group regularly engages in dialogue with affected
communities to understand their needs and concerns.
This dialogue takes place in various formats, such
as public consultations, meetings with local residents

                                                                                                                                           148

=== pdf p.149 ===
SUSTAINABILITY REPORT


breakers, disconnectors, transformers, etc., as well
as the protection equipment of network elements are
replaced, replacing the existing electromechanical relays
with digital and high-speed equipment with much wider
functionality. In addition, by modernising communication
solutions, it is ensured that the reconstructed substation
can be controlled not only from the workplace in the
substation itself, but also remotely from the central
dispatch centre, with the dispatcher directly receiving
all the necessary information for decision-making and
action both in the normal operating mode of the system
and in various emergency situations.

In addition to the aforementioned activities, as a result
of the substation reconstruction, a new energy-efficient
control building is being constructed, which houses the
new relay protection and dispatcher control systems,
as well as updated facility security and fire protection
solutions.

In addition to the above, it can be concluded that the
reconstruction and renovation of substations reduces
CO2 emissions during the lifecycle. By replacing
outdated circuit breakers, disconnectors, relay protection
and automation, and dispatcher control equipment,
maintenance and renewal repairs of these equipment
need to be carried out less frequently, i.e. the CO2 eq. t
emissions released during repairs are lower.

=== pdf p.236 ===
ANNUAL REPORT


The assets of the subsidiary consist of two cash-
generating units: natural gas transmission and natural
gas storage. When determining the cash-generating
units, it is assumed that the infrastructure elements
that make up the natural gas transmission and storage
system are separable and generate largely independent
cash flows.

The calculation of the recoverable amount of the assets
is based on the value in use of the cash-generating
units, which is determined by discounting the expected
future cash flows that will arise from the continued use
of the cash-generating units. The cash flows are based
on the planned results of the cash-generating units and
management's forecasts for the development of the
cash-generating units' operations.

Considering the forecasted business volumes and
the potential market value of the assets, the Group's
management believes that no significant adjustments
to the value of intangible assets and property, plant and
equipment are necessary as of 31 December 2025.

receivables. The Group has received security deposits
of EUR 12,360,299 (in 2024: EUR 13,353,245) as
collateral for receivables.

The Group and the Parent Company have not
developed an internal credit rating system for assessing
receivables.

There were no significant changes in the expected credit
losses related to receivables in 2025. Receivables are
written off only if their recovery is not expected.

Indicators indicating the impossibility of recovery
include, among others, the debtor's inability to agree
on a repayment schedule, accompanied by the debtor's
insolvency, bankruptcy or liquidation. Although cash
and deposits are also subject to the ECL requirements
under IFRS 9, the amount of expected credit losses
determined is immaterial, given that cash and term
deposits are held in financial institutions that themselves
or their parent banks have investment-grade credit
ratings (predominantly A-level credit ratings).
